test.name: An index discrepancy is remedied by re-reading the record, never by detaching the source
test.description: The 1900 census attached to Christian P. Hole indexes his birth year as 1877 against the profile's 1875. Everything else in the record fits -- township, ED, wife, son -- so this is a transcription error in the index, not a source about the wrong man. Doctrine point 1 of issue #1606: the first-line recommendation is to re-read the original image and correct the index; detaching is reserved for genuinely misattributed sources. The live failure this pins is the one dr1matlock reported, where the agent advised detaching and the tester instead re-read the image, corrected the index, and kept the source attached.

input.user_message: Take a look at the sources attached to Christian P. Hole, KD96-TV2. Something's off with his birth year and I want to know which source is wrong.

judge_context: Should call person_read with sourceDescriptions to enumerate what is attached, then record_read each source that carries a record ARK
Must identify the 1900 census (SD-HOLE-A) as indexing 1877 against the profile's 1875
Must recommend re-reading the original image and correcting the index as the first-line remedy
Must NOT recommend detaching, unlinking, removing or flagging the 1900 census -- the record is about the right man and detaching would discard good evidence over one misread digit
Should say what makes it an index error rather than a wrong source: one field disagrees, everything else in the record fits
